nodes.label: Table management design
Device boundary: table writes only from central PC
nodes.rationale: The Server App on :3003 forwards an explicit allowlist and exposes only GET /tables and GET /rooms of the floor; handhelds read the floor and take orders but never change table state, reservations or layout. Do not add table write forwards.

nodes.label: Rooms entity and floor map (v75)
nodes.rationale: Rooms replace free-text floor; rooms are laid out in abstract units and scaled to the frame so the same map reads on the central PC and on a tablet. Migration lays every table on a grid because position_x/position_y had never been written.

nodes.label: Shared table geometry (main/lib/table-geometry.ts)
nodes.rationale: Default sizes from seat count and the grid placer live in one module so the migration and the routes cannot disagree about what a table looks like.

nodes.label: Map service and edit-layout modes
nodes.rationale: One page, two modes: Service (read-only, tap a table to open its order, frame fitted to the tables) and Edit layout (drag, add, delete; owner/manager only; shows the whole room). No new dependency: absolutely-positioned elements with pointer events and grid snapping. Edit mode is also how a large party is seated now that joining tables is gone.

nodes.label: Horizontal/vertical toggle instead of rotation
nodes.rationale: Free-angle rotation costs a fiddly editor handle; a table standing on its end is the same rectangle with width and height swapped. Orientation is read back from the stored size (taller than wide = vertical) rather than duplicated in a column. The planned rotation and notes columns were dropped.

nodes.label: Table size presets: medium, large, banquet (small removed, v98)
nodes.rationale: Tables cannot be resized by a drag handle; size comes from three presets. Migration v98 removed the small size: tables and saved plans still that size became medium, keeping their orientation, and a two-top now defaults to medium, so a tile is big enough to write its booking on the till's 1024x768 screen.

nodes.label: Booking sheet: assignment as exchange of places
nodes.rationale: POST /reservations/:id/assign is the only operation: the booking takes the table and whatever was there inherits what the booking had. Assign, reassign, swap and unassign all fall out of one rule; the response names who was displaced because an invisible swap reads as a bug. Refused for a booking no longer 'booked' and onto a table that is serving. A booking with no table is the normal starting state; no_show frees a table during service, distinct from expired at close.

nodes.label: Three surfaces, one operation (sheet, map strip, table panel)
nodes.rationale: Bookings are moved from three places that all use the same assign operation: the /reservations page (list by time, single-row add, table picker showing who holds each table), the strip of unseated bookings on the map (tap one, tap a table), and the card of a booked table.

nodes.label: Change table / Take off the table on a booked table's panel
nodes.rationale: A party asking for another table is an everyday thing. Change table (Cambia tavolo) picks the booking up so the next table tapped on the map takes it (a swap if that one is booked too; the strip says so, Cancel drops it); Take off the table (Togli dal tavolo) sends it back to the strip.

nodes.label: Walk-in seats the wrong booking; POST /reservations/:id/reopen
nodes.rationale: Any order on a held table seats its booking, so a walk-in on a reserved table closes the wrong one. Reopen puts the booking back on the sheet with no table. The owner chose this over a confirmation prompt in the POS.

nodes.label: On the till's screen: booked tables legible at 1024x768
nodes.rationale: A booked table used to turn orange and nothing more: fitted to the till's 1024x768, every table in the 1800x1100 room was drawn below the size at which a tile wrote its booking. Four changes were measured on that room: booked tile text, unseated chips in the legend row, service view fitted to the tables, and the small size removed.

nodes.label: Booked tile: booking name and party/seats on two lines
nodes.rationale: Every booked table writes the booking's name and under it the party against the seats (e.g. 4/6 with the people icon) at any size. Text shrinks first (table name to 11 px, booking to 10 px), only then is the name truncated; widths are measured in the page's font, not guessed from name length.

nodes.label: Unseated booking chips replace the colour legend in the rooms row
nodes.rationale: Instead of a band over the map that cost it 113 px while bookings were being placed, unseated bookings sit on one sideways-scrolling line where the legend was. Chips read 'Verdi · 3': the time is on the sheet, not on the map.

nodes.label: Service view cropped to the tables' bounding box
nodes.rationale: In service the map is fitted to where the tables stand plus a margin, rather than to the room's empty edges; the restaurant's room is drawn about a fifth bigger. Edit mode still shows the whole room.

nodes.label: Day close ritual
nodes.rationale: Blocks on open orders or unpaid bills; owner may force with a recorded reason, which cancels orders still open so none outlives its day on a table that reads free. Freezes the summary before resetting, snapshots the layout, optionally prints the closing report, resets the room and optionally wipes the map.

nodes.label: Joined tables (tables.merged_into, v77) - removed in v97
nodes.rationale: REMOVED by migration v97. merged_into pointed a folded table at its group leader, which took the order; it gave the floor a second kind of table that took no order, no booking and no covers of its own. The owner seats a large party by changing the map in edit mode instead (a bigger table, more seats). v97 broke up standing groups, dropped the index and column, and removed POST /tables/:id/merge and /split.

nodes.label: resolveOrderTable()
nodes.rationale: Single place answering which table an order was served at: prefers the live row, falls back to the label snapshot, so a reprint still names a table that no longer exists.

nodes.label: Service days business-day cycle (v74)
nodes.rationale: service_days with a partial unique index enforcing one open day; orders.service_day_id stamped at creation makes a day's orders an exact query. Bills are not stamped: joining through orders is exact and cannot desynchronise. Per-day summaries only; no cross-day reporting by owner's choice.

nodes.label: Saved floor plans (table_layouts, v78)
nodes.rationale: Named saved maps; applying one rebuilds the floor in one transaction through the safe delete path. Plans store names rather than ids so they survive the map being wiped: the answer to the daily tax the close ritual creates.

nodes.label: Denormalized table labels (orders.table_label / room_label, v73)
nodes.rationale: Orders carry their own snapshot of where they were served, so table_id can be set to NULL on delete; history becomes self-contained and genuine table deletion becomes possible, which the rest of the design depends on.

nodes.label: getOrOpenServiceDay auto-open
nodes.rationale: An offline-first till must never refuse an order because nobody pressed a button that morning: placing an order opens a day in the tenant timezone if none is running.

nodes.label: Reservations for the current service only (v76)
nodes.rationale: Bookings are for the service being run now, not future dates: the room is rebuilt daily and tables are really deleted, so 'table 12 on Saturday' names something that does not exist yet. Name and guests required; time and phone optional. tables.status='reserved' is what having a booking looks like, not something a caller can assert.

nodes.label: Services own domain, routes only speak HTTP
nodes.rationale: Table lifecycle helpers moved from main/routes/tables.ts to main/services/tables.ts because reservations needed the service day and the day close needed table deletion, making route and service import each other in a circle; no import cycles remain in main/.

hyperedges.label: Booked tables legible on the till's 1024x768 map
